title: T-Shirt Cleaning Towel
summary: Cut an old tee into an absorbent, washable towel for everyday cleaning.
tools: Fabric glue or needle and thread

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Prepare your old T-shirt
- Scissors
- Ruler
- Fabric clips or pins to help you cut the fabric evenly.
steps.tip: Choose a T-shirt made of absorbent fabric, such as cotton, for better cleaning results

steps.title: Cut the Fabric
steps.heading: Shape Your Towel:
steps.detail: Lay the T-shirt flat and cut the fabric into a rectangular shape using scissors. Avoid seams and thick areas for a smoother towel.
steps.tip: Use a ruler to measure your desired towel size before cutting

steps.title: Finish the Edges
steps.heading: Make It Neat:
steps.detail: Fold the raw edges inward and secure them with fabric glue or sew them to prevent fraying.
steps.tip: Keep the edges even for a neat, durable towel

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old T-shirt is now a cleaning towel! Use it to wipe surfaces and handle everyday cleaning tasks.
steps.tip: Wash the towel after use and reuse it whenever needed

benefit: Keeps fabric in use and cuts down on single-use paper towels.

title: No-Sew T-Shirt Tote
summary: Turn a tee into a stretchy market bag with nothing but scissors and knots.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old T-shirt (thicker cotton works best)
- Fabric scissors
- Ruler
- Chalk or a washable marker
steps.tip: Turn the T-shirt inside out first so the knots end up hidden

steps.title: Shape the Bag
steps.heading: Make the Handles:
steps.detail: Cut both sleeves off just inside the seam, then cut a U-shape around the neckline about 8 cm deep through both layers.
steps.tip: Fold the shirt in half lengthwise so both sides match

steps.title: Knot the Bottom
steps.heading: Close It Up:
steps.detail: Cut strips 2 cm wide and 8 cm tall along the hem through both layers, then tie each front strip to the back strip below it.
steps.tip: Double-knot every pair so heavier shopping can't slip through

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old T-shirt is now a tote bag! Turn it right side out and take it shopping.
steps.tip: Wash it inside a laundry bag so the knots stay tight

benefit: Gives a worn tee years of extra use and replaces new reusable bags.

title: T-Shirt Yarn
summary: Cut one continuous strip from a tee and roll it into chunky craft yarn.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old T-shirt (seamless sides are best)
- Fabric scissors
- Ruler
steps.tip: Stretchy jersey makes the smoothest yarn

steps.title: Cut the Loops
steps.heading: Prepare the Body:
steps.detail: Cut off the hem and everything above the armpits. Fold the tube in half, then cut 2 cm strips, stopping 3 cm before the fold.
steps.tip: Keep your strips the same width for even yarn

steps.title: Make One Strip
steps.heading: Cut Diagonally:
steps.detail: Open the uncut band and cut diagonally from the edge to the first slit, then on to each next slit, so the loops become one long strip.
steps.tip: Pull the strip gently as you go so the edges curl into yarn

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old T-shirt is now T-shirt yarn! Roll it into a ball and crochet a basket, coaster or rug.
steps.tip: Join a second shirt's yarn with a small knot to keep going

benefit: Even stained or holey tees become a craft material instead of waste.

title: Raw-Edge Crop Top
summary: Give a tee you never reach for a fresh, cropped shape.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old T-shirt
- Fabric scissors
- Chalk
- Ruler
steps.tip: Try the T-shirt on first and decide where you want it to end

steps.title: Mark the Length
steps.heading: Measure Twice:
steps.detail: Put the T-shirt on, mark the new hem with chalk, then lay it flat and draw a straight line across both layers.
steps.tip: Leave 2 cm extra — jersey curls up after washing

steps.title: Cut the Hem
steps.heading: One Clean Cut:
steps.detail: Cut along the chalk line through both layers in one smooth motion.
steps.tip: Stretch the new edge gently to make it roll softly

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old T-shirt is now a crop top! Style it over high-waisted jeans or a skirt.
steps.tip: Save the cut-off band — it makes a great headband

benefit: Restyles an under-worn tee into something you'll actually reach for.

title: Drawstring Pouch
summary: Sew a small pouch for chargers, toiletries or snacks.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old garment
- A shoelace or cord (about 60 cm)
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- Safety pin
steps.tip: Use the least damaged area of the fabric for the pouch

steps.title: Cut and Sew
steps.heading: Make the Pouch:
steps.detail: Cut two 20 × 25 cm rectangles. Place them right sides together and sew around the sides and bottom, 1 cm from the edge.
steps.tip: Leave the top open — that's where the drawstring goes

steps.title: Add the Drawstring
steps.heading: Make the Channel:
steps.detail: Fold the top edge down 2 cm and stitch it to form a channel. Pin the cord to a safety pin and thread it through.
steps.tip: Leave a small gap in the channel so the cord can come out

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old garment is now a drawstring pouch! Fill it and pull the cord closed.
steps.tip: Make a few in different sizes for packing

benefit: Uses offcuts and replaces small plastic pouches or zip bags.

title: Denim Tote Bag
summary: Turn the legs of old jeans into a strong everyday tote.
tools: Needle and strong thread or a sewing machine

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jeans
- Fabric scissors
- Strong thread and needle (or a sewing machine)
- Pins
- Ruler
steps.tip: Denim is thick — use a denim needle if you sew by machine

steps.title: Cut the Panels
steps.heading: Shape Your Bag:
steps.detail: Cut both legs open along the inner seam and cut two 35 × 40 cm panels, plus two 6 × 60 cm strips for handles.
steps.tip: Keep a back pocket on one panel for a built-in pocket

steps.title: Sew It Together
steps.heading: Join and Attach:
steps.detail: Sew the panels right sides together on three sides. Fold and stitch the handle strips, then sew them inside the top edge.
steps.tip: Stitch a box with an X over each handle for extra strength

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jeans are now a denim tote! Turn it right side out and fill it up.
steps.tip: Denim softens with every wash — it only gets better

benefit: Denim is durable — this keeps it in use for years instead of landfill.

title: Jeans to Mini Skirt
summary: Open the leg seams and turn jeans into a fitted mini skirt.
tools: Sewing machine or needle and thread

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jeans
- Seam ripper
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Sewing machine or needle and thread
steps.tip: Jeans that fit well at the waist make the best skirts

steps.title: Open the Seams
steps.heading: Unpick and Cut:
steps.detail: Cut the legs off at your chosen length plus 3 cm. Unpick the inner leg seams and the curved crotch seam.
steps.tip: Take your time with the seam ripper — clean seams lie flatter

steps.title: Fill the Gaps
steps.heading: Sew the Panels:
steps.detail: Lay the front flat so it overlaps, pin a triangle of leftover denim behind the front and back gaps, and topstitch it in place.
steps.tip: Match the thread colour to the original jeans stitching

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jeans are now a mini skirt! Trim the hem and wash it to fray the edge.
steps.tip: Wear it with the tee you cropped for a full upcycled look

benefit: Gives jeans that no longer fit at the leg a completely new look.

title: Cut-Off Shorts
summary: Rescue jeans or trousers with damaged knees by cutting them into shorts.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jeans or trousers
- Fabric scissors
- Chalk
- Ruler
steps.tip: Damaged knees? Cut above them and the damage disappears

steps.title: Mark the Length
steps.heading: Measure First:
steps.detail: Try them on, mark your length with chalk, then add 3 cm. Fold one leg over the other so both match.
steps.tip: Cut slightly longer than you think — you can always trim more

steps.title: Cut the Legs
steps.heading: Make the Cut:
steps.detail: Cut straight across both legs along your line, angling slightly lower at the outer seam.
steps.tip: Roll the hem twice for a neat cuff instead of a fray

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old trousers are now shorts! Wash them once to soften the edge.
steps.tip: Keep the cut-off legs for patches or a pouch

benefit: Rescues trousers with damaged knees or hems.

title: Patchwork Mending Patches
summary: Cut sturdy patches from jeans to repair other clothes.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jeans or jacket
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and embroidery thread
- Pins
steps.tip: Look for areas with no holes — the back of the leg is ideal

steps.title: Cut the Patches
steps.heading: Make a Stack:
steps.detail: Cut squares and rectangles 2 cm larger than the holes you want to cover, rounding the corners slightly.
steps.tip: Rounded corners stop patches from peeling up

steps.title: Stitch a Patch On
steps.heading: Mend Something:
steps.detail: Pin a patch behind or over a hole on another garment and sew around the edge with small running stitches.
steps.tip: Use a contrast thread colour to make the mend a feature

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jeans are now mending patches! Keep the rest in a pouch for the next repair.
steps.tip: One pair of jeans can mend a whole wardrobe

benefit: Mending extends the life of other clothes — one old item helps many.

title: Button-Front Pillow Cover
summary: Use the shirt's own buttons as the opening of a cushion cover.
tools: Needle and thread or sewing machine

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old button-up shirt
- A cushion insert
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Needle and thread
steps.tip: Button the shirt up before you start so the front lines up

steps.title: Cut the Square
steps.heading: Frame the Buttons:
steps.detail: Lay the cushion on the buttoned shirt with the buttons in the middle. Cut a square 2 cm larger than the cushion through both layers.
steps.tip: Keep the pocket on the front for a playful detail

steps.title: Sew the Edges
steps.heading: Close the Sides:
steps.detail: Turn the shirt inside out, pin the four edges and sew them 1 cm from the edge.
steps.tip: Clip the corners before turning it right side out

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shirt is now a pillow cover! Unbutton it, slip in the cushion and button it up.
steps.tip: Plaid and striped shirts look great as cushions

benefit: Refreshes your space with a piece that already has a story.

title: Shirt Market Bag
summary: Turn a roomy shirt or dress into a light, foldable shopping bag.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shirt or dress
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Needle and thread
steps.tip: Lightweight fabric folds small enough to carry in a pocket

steps.title: Cut the Shape
steps.heading: Make the Handles:
steps.detail: Cut off the sleeves and cut a deep U-shape around the collar. The shoulders become the handles.
steps.tip: Fold the shirt in half first so the shape is even

steps.title: Sew the Bottom
steps.heading: Close It Up:
steps.detail: Turn it inside out and sew straight across the hem. Then fold and stitch the raw armhole edges.
steps.tip: Sew across the bottom twice so it can carry heavier items

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shirt is now a market bag! Turn it right side out and fold it into its own pocket.
steps.tip: Keep it in your bag so you never need a plastic one

benefit: Replaces a new reusable bag with one made from fabric you already have.

title: Sleeve-Tie Shirt Skirt
summary: Wrap a shirt around your waist and tie the sleeves — no cutting at all.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old button-up shirt (oversized works best)
- A mirror
steps.tip: No cutting — the shirt stays a shirt whenever you want

steps.title: Button and Wrap
steps.heading: Set the Waist:
steps.detail: Button the shirt fully, step into it and pull it up to your waist with the collar hanging inside.
steps.tip: Tuck the collar in so it doesn't show at the back

steps.title: Tie the Sleeves
steps.heading: Make the Bow:
steps.detail: Bring the sleeves around your waist and tie them in a knot or bow at the front or side.
steps.tip: Roll the sleeves first for a neater knot

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shirt is now a wrap skirt! Pair it with a fitted top.
steps.tip: Try it with the buttons at the back for a different look

benefit: A reversible restyle — no cuts, so the shirt stays a shirt too.

title: Sleeve Fingerless Gloves
summary: Cut the cuffs of a sweater into cosy fingerless gloves.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old sweater
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- Chalk
steps.tip: Cuffs with ribbing make the snuggest gloves

steps.title: Cut the Sleeves
steps.heading: Measure Your Hand:
steps.detail: Slip a sleeve on, mark from the cuff to just past your knuckles and cut both sleeves at that length.
steps.tip: Sew around a knit edge right away so it doesn't unravel

steps.title: Make a Thumb Hole
steps.heading: Shape the Glove:
steps.detail: Put it on, mark where your thumb sits, cut a 3 cm slit and stitch around the slit to stop fraying.
steps.tip: Use a blanket stitch for a neat edge

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old sweater is now fingerless gloves! Wear them on cold mornings.
steps.tip: Hand wash to keep the knit soft

benefit: Saves a knit that can't be worn as-is and keeps you warm without buying new.

title: Knit Cushion Cover
summary: Turn a cosy sweater into a soft cushion cover.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old sweater
- A cushion insert
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Needle and thread
steps.tip: Choose a cushion that fits inside the sweater body

steps.title: Cut the Square
steps.heading: Frame the Pattern:
steps.detail: Turn the sweater inside out, lay the cushion on it and cut a square 2 cm larger than the cushion through both layers.
steps.tip: Centre any pattern or cable knit on the front

steps.title: Sew Three Sides
steps.heading: Close It Up:
steps.detail: Pin and sew three sides, turn it right side out, insert the cushion and hand-sew the last side closed.
steps.tip: Use small stitches so the knit doesn't stretch

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old sweater is now a cushion cover! Add it to your sofa or bed.
steps.tip: Use the sleeves to make a matching smaller cushion

benefit: Keeps a beloved knit around even when it no longer fits.

title: Dress to Top
summary: Cut a dress that no longer works into a top you'll actually wear.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old dress
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Needle and thread
- Chalk
steps.tip: Damage at the hem? This idea cuts it away

steps.title: Mark the Length
steps.heading: Find the New Hem:
steps.detail: Put the dress on, mark where you want the top to end and add 3 cm for the hem. Cut straight across.
steps.tip: Lay it flat and use a ruler so the hem is level

steps.title: Hem the Edge
steps.heading: Make It Neat:
steps.detail: Fold the raw edge under twice by 1.5 cm, pin and stitch it all the way around.
steps.tip: Iron the fold first for a crisp hem

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old dress is now a top! Tuck it into jeans or a skirt.
steps.tip: Use the leftover skirt fabric for a matching scrunchie

benefit: Turns a special-occasion piece into something you can rewear often.

title: Twisted Scarf Headband
summary: Twist a forgotten scarf into a bold headband.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old scarf
- A mirror
- Hair pins
steps.tip: Silky square scarves twist the most neatly

steps.title: Fold the Scarf
steps.heading: Make a Band:
steps.detail: Fold the scarf into a triangle, then fold from the long edge in 4 cm sections until it is a long band.
steps.tip: Keep folds flat so the band doesn't bulge

steps.title: Twist and Tie
steps.heading: Shape It:
steps.detail: Place the middle at the nape of your neck, bring the ends up, twist them together on top and tuck them under.
steps.tip: Secure the ends with two hair pins

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old scarf is now a headband! Wear it with your hair up or down.
steps.tip: Try a knot at the front for a retro look

benefit: A new way to wear an accessory that's been sitting in a drawer.

title: Sneaker Planter
summary: Plant herbs or succulents in shoes that can't be worn anymore.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shoes
- Potting soil
- A small plant or seeds
- Small stones
- Scissors or a screwdriver
steps.tip: Canvas sneakers and boots hold the most soil

steps.title: Prepare the Shoe
steps.heading: Make Drainage:
steps.detail: Remove the laces and insole. Make a few small holes in the sole and add a layer of stones at the bottom.
steps.tip: Drainage keeps the roots from rotting

steps.title: Plant It
steps.heading: Add Soil and Plant:
steps.detail: Fill the shoe with soil, make a hole, place the plant and press the soil gently around it.
steps.tip: Succulents need the least care

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shoes are now a planter! Put it on a sunny windowsill or balcony.
steps.tip: Water lightly — shoes dry slower than pots

benefit: Gives unwearable shoes a fun second life at home.

title: Fabric Scrap Bunting
summary: Turn even small or stained pieces into colourful party bunting.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old garment
- A long ribbon or string
- Fabric scissors
- Cardboard for a template
- Fabric glue
steps.tip: Mix several old garments for colourful bunting

steps.title: Cut the Flags
steps.heading: Make a Template:
steps.detail: Cut a triangle 15 cm wide and 20 cm tall from cardboard, trace it on the fabric and cut out as many flags as you can.
steps.tip: Cut around stains — they won't show

steps.title: Attach the Flags
steps.heading: String Them Up:
steps.detail: Fold the top of each flag over the string by 1 cm and glue it closed, leaving 5 cm between flags.
steps.tip: Let the glue dry flat for an hour

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old garment is now bunting! Hang it at a party or in your room.
steps.tip: Reuse it for every celebration instead of buying decorations

benefit: Uses up even small or stained pieces and replaces single-use decorations.

title: Cosy Pet Bed
summary: Stuff a jacket or hoodie into a soft bed for a cat or small dog.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jacket or hoodie
- An old pillow or stuffing
- Needle and thread
- Safety pins
steps.tip: Soft linings and fleece make the cosiest beds

steps.title: Close the Openings
steps.heading: Seal It Up:
steps.detail: Zip or button the jacket closed, then sew the neck opening and the bottom hem shut, leaving one sleeve open.
steps.tip: Safety-pin first, then sew, so nothing shifts

steps.title: Stuff and Shape
steps.heading: Make the Bed:
steps.detail: Push the stuffing into the body. Stuff the sleeves too, then curve them around the body and stitch the cuffs together.
steps.tip: The sleeves become a bolster pets love to lean on

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jacket is now a pet bed! Place it somewhere warm and quiet.
steps.tip: Remove the stuffing to wash the cover

benefit: Gives outerwear that can't be worn a cosy second life.

title: Belt Key Holder
summary: Cut an old belt into a wall strap that holds keys and small things.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old belt
- Scissors
- Two screws and a screwdriver
- Key rings or small S-hooks
steps.tip: Thick leather belts make the strongest holders

steps.title: Cut the Strap
steps.heading: Choose the Length:
steps.detail: Cut a 25 cm piece that includes three or four of the belt holes.
steps.tip: Keep the buckle end as a decorative loop

steps.title: Fix It to the Wall
steps.heading: Mount It:
steps.detail: Screw both ends of the strap to the wall or a door, leaving it slightly loose so it forms a loop.
steps.tip: Check for pipes or wires before you drill

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old belt is now a key holder! Hang key rings from the belt holes.
steps.tip: Make a second one for headphones or sunglasses

benefit: Keeps a worn belt useful instead of throwing it away.

title: Shorts Wall Organizer
summary: Hang old shorts flat on the wall and use their pockets for small things.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shorts (or jeans cut at the knee)
- A wooden dowel or a trouser hanger
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- Two nails or adhesive hooks
steps.tip: Shorts with four working pockets hold the most

steps.title: Close the Legs
steps.heading: Make a Flat Panel:
steps.detail: Turn the shorts inside out and sew straight across both leg openings, so the shorts become one flat panel with pockets.
steps.tip: Iron the panel flat before sewing for a neat finish

steps.title: Hang It Up
steps.heading: Mount the Panel:
steps.detail: Slide a dowel through the belt loops or clip the waistband to a trouser hanger, then hang it on two nails or hooks.
steps.tip: Hang it at eye level so the back pockets are easy to reach

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shorts are now a wall organizer! Fill the pockets with keys, chargers, letters or pens.
steps.tip: Add a small label to each pocket so everyone knows where things go

benefit: Keeps sturdy fabric and pockets in use instead of throwing them away.

title: Shorts Shoulder Bag
summary: Sew the legs closed and add a strap to make a casual bag with built-in pockets.
materials: A strap, belt or the cut-off waistband of another garment

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shorts
- A strap or an old belt
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and strong thread
- Pins
steps.tip: Shorts with a zip fly make a bag that closes

steps.title: Sew the Bottom
steps.heading: Close the Legs:
steps.detail: Turn the shorts inside out, pin the leg openings shut and sew one straight seam across both legs, 1 cm from the edge.
steps.tip: Sew the seam twice — the bottom carries all the weight

steps.title: Add the Strap
steps.heading: Attach It:
steps.detail: Turn the shorts right side out, thread the strap through the belt loops on each side and knot or stitch the ends in place.
steps.tip: Make the strap long enough to wear across your body

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shorts are now a shoulder bag! Use the pockets for your phone and keys.
steps.tip: Wash it inside out on a gentle cycle

benefit: Turns shorts that no longer fit into a bag you can use every day.

title: Jumpsuit to Separates
summary: Cut a jumpsuit at the waist to get a top and trousers you can mix with the rest of your wardrobe.
materials: Elastic, 2.5 cm wide, your waist length
tools: Sewing machine or needle and thread

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jumpsuit
- Wide elastic (your waist measurement)
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread or a sewing machine
- Safety pin
- Chalk
steps.tip: Jumpsuits with a waist seam are the easiest to split

steps.title: Cut at the Waist
steps.heading: Separate the Halves:
steps.detail: Mark a line 3 cm below the waist seam with chalk and cut around the jumpsuit along it.
steps.tip: Cut below the seam so the trousers keep enough fabric for a casing

steps.title: Finish Both Edges
steps.heading: Hem and Add Elastic:
steps.detail: Hem the bottom of the top. On the trousers, fold the edge over 3 cm, stitch it to make a casing and thread the elastic through with a safety pin.
steps.tip: Overlap the elastic ends by 2 cm and stitch them firmly before closing the casing

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jumpsuit is now a top and trousers! Wear them together or with other pieces.
steps.tip: Try the top over a skirt for a new outfit

benefit: Doubles the number of outfits a jumpsuit can make.

title: Sleeve Draught Stopper
summary: Stuff a coat or sweater sleeve to stop cold air coming under a door.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old coat, jacket or sweater
- Old socks, rags or stuffing
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
steps.tip: Heavy wool and padded sleeves block the most draught

steps.title: Cut the Sleeves
steps.heading: Make the Tube:
steps.detail: Cut both sleeves off at the shoulder seam and sew one sleeve to the other at the wide ends to make one long tube.
steps.tip: Measure your door — the tube should be as wide as the doorway

steps.title: Stuff and Close
steps.heading: Fill It Up:
steps.detail: Sew one cuff shut, push the stuffing in until the tube is firm, then sew the other cuff closed.
steps.tip: Add a handful of dry rice at the ends to help it stay in place

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old coat is now a draught stopper! Lay it along the bottom of a door or window.
steps.tip: Keeping draughts out means less heating — good for the planet and your bills

benefit: Turns a worn coat into something that saves heating energy.

title: Padded Laptop Sleeve
summary: Use the sturdy front of a blazer or coat, buttons and all, as a laptop or tablet case.
tools: Needle and thread or a sewing machine

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old blazer, coat or jacket
- Your laptop or tablet to measure
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- Pins
- Ruler
steps.tip: Keep the lining — it protects the screen

steps.title: Measure and Cut
steps.heading: Size the Sleeve:
steps.detail: Button the garment and lay your laptop on the front. Cut a rectangle 4 cm bigger than the laptop on every side through both front and back, keeping the buttons in the middle.
steps.tip: Measure twice — the laptop should slide in snugly

steps.title: Sew the Sides
steps.heading: Close It Up:
steps.detail: Turn it inside out, pin and sew the top, bottom and back edges, then turn it right side out. The buttons become the opening.
steps.tip: Use small, tight stitches at the corners, where the laptop pushes hardest

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old blazer is now a laptop sleeve! Unbutton it to slide your laptop in.
steps.tip: Keep your charger in the original breast pocket

benefit: Keeps tailored fabric in use and replaces a new store-bought case.

title: Jacket to Vest
summary: Remove the sleeves of a jacket or blazer for a layering vest.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old jacket or blazer
- Fabric scissors
- Seam ripper
- Needle and thread
- Pins
steps.tip: Damaged or stained sleeves? This is the perfect fix

steps.title: Remove the Sleeves
steps.heading: Cut Them Off:
steps.detail: Cut each sleeve off 1.5 cm outside the shoulder seam, or unpick the seam with a seam ripper for a cleaner edge.
steps.tip: Denim looks great with a raw edge — you can stop here

steps.title: Finish the Armholes
steps.heading: Neat Edges:
steps.detail: Fold the raw edge inward by 1 cm, pin it all around and hand-stitch it in place.
steps.tip: Clip the curve every few centimetres so it folds flat

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old jacket is now a vest! Layer it over a shirt or hoodie.
steps.tip: Use the cut sleeves to make patches or a pouch

benefit: Saves a jacket with worn sleeves and keeps it in your wardrobe.

title: Boot Vase
summary: Hide a jar inside a boot or high-top sneaker for a quirky flower vase.
materials: A tall glass jar or bottle

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old boot or high-top sneaker
- A tall jar or bottle that fits inside
- Flowers
- Small stones
steps.tip: Ankle and tall boots fit a jar best

steps.title: Fit the Jar
steps.heading: Make It Stable:
steps.detail: Remove the laces or insole if needed. Put a few stones in the toe and stand the jar upright inside the boot shaft.
steps.tip: Stones in the toe stop the boot from tipping over

steps.title: Add Flowers
steps.heading: Fill the Vase:
steps.detail: Fill the jar with water and arrange your flowers inside.
steps.tip: Use dried flowers if the boot is suede or leather — no spill worries

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old boot is now a vase! Put it by the door or on a shelf.
steps.tip: Swap the flowers with the seasons

benefit: Gives a single boot or worn-out pair a decorative second life.

title: Shoe Jewellery Stand
summary: Turn a heel, flat or sandal into a stand for rings, bracelets and necklaces.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shoe
- Paint and a paintbrush
- Small cup hooks
- Strong glue or a hot-glue gun
steps.tip: High heels give the most hanging space

steps.title: Paint the Shoe
steps.heading: Give It a New Look:
steps.detail: Wipe the shoe clean, then paint it in one bold colour. Let it dry and add a second coat.
steps.tip: Spray paint covers leather and fabric most evenly — use it outdoors

steps.title: Add the Hooks
steps.heading: Make Places to Hang:
steps.detail: Screw or glue small hooks along the heel and the edge of the sole. Rings sit on the heel; necklaces hang from the hooks.
steps.tip: Space the hooks 2 cm apart so chains don't tangle

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shoe is now a jewellery stand! Put it on your dresser and hang your favourite pieces.
steps.tip: Make a pair — one for rings, one for necklaces

benefit: Turns a single shoe or broken pair into a statement storage piece.

title: Shoe Doorstop
summary: Fill an old shoe with a sealed bag of sand or rice so it holds a door open.
tools: Needle and strong thread or strong glue

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shoe
- About 1 kg of sand, rice or stones
- A sturdy zip bag
- Needle and strong thread or strong glue
steps.tip: Heavier shoes like boots hold doors best

steps.title: Fill the Weight Bag
steps.heading: Add the Weight:
steps.detail: Fill the bag with sand or rice, squeeze the air out and seal it. Push it into the shoe, deep into the toe.
steps.tip: Double-bag the sand so it can never leak

steps.title: Close the Shoe
steps.heading: Seal the Top:
steps.detail: Lace the shoe tightly, or sew or glue a piece of fabric across the opening so the bag stays inside.
steps.tip: An old sock pulled over the opening also works

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shoe is now a doorstop! Put it against a door to hold it open.
steps.tip: Paint it or add a fun lace to match your room

benefit: A heavy, worn shoe becomes a useful object instead of waste.

title: Shoelace Key Lanyard
summary: Braid old shoelaces into a strong lanyard for keys or a badge.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Three shoelaces (from one or more pairs)
- A key ring
- Scissors
- Tape
- Clear nail polish
steps.tip: Mix colours for a bold braid

steps.title: Braid the Laces
steps.heading: Make the Cord:
steps.detail: Tape the three laces together at one end and braid them tightly until you reach about 45 cm.
steps.tip: Tape the start to a table to keep the braid tight

steps.title: Close the Loop
steps.heading: Add the Ring:
steps.detail: Thread the braid through the key ring, fold it into a loop and tie the two ends together with a double knot. Trim and seal the ends with nail polish.
steps.tip: Sealing stops the ends from fraying

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old laces are now a key lanyard! Clip your keys on and wear it round your neck or wrist.
steps.tip: Make extras as gifts for friends

benefit: Uses the part of a shoe that usually gets thrown away first.

title: Leather Strap Keyrings
summary: Cut the straps of worn sandals, heels or boots into leather keyrings.
materials: Your old shoes with leather straps
tools: Leather hole punch or a nail and hammer

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old shoes with leather straps or tabs
- Key rings
- Sharp scissors
- Leather hole punch (or a nail and hammer)
steps.tip: Thicker straps make sturdier keyrings

steps.title: Cut the Straps
steps.heading: Free the Leather:
steps.detail: Cut the straps off the sole and trim each one into a 10 × 2 cm piece with rounded ends.
steps.tip: Round the corners so the keyring doesn't scratch your pocket

steps.title: Punch and Attach
steps.heading: Add the Ring:
steps.detail: Fold each piece in half, punch a hole through both ends and fix them onto a key ring.
steps.tip: Add a rivet or a few stitches for extra hold

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old shoes are now keyrings! Keep one and give the rest away.
steps.tip: Mark each keyring with a pen to tell your keys apart

benefit: Saves good leather from shoes that can't be worn anymore.

title: Hanging Bag Planter
summary: Line an old tote or handbag and hang it as a planter for herbs.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old tote or handbag
- A plastic liner (an old bag works)
- Potting soil
- Herbs or seeds
- Scissors
- A sturdy hook
steps.tip: Canvas and fabric bags let the roots breathe

steps.title: Line the Bag
steps.heading: Prepare It:
steps.detail: Put the liner inside the bag and poke a few small holes in its bottom for drainage.
steps.tip: Add a layer of small stones before the soil

steps.title: Plant It
steps.heading: Add Soil and Plants:
steps.detail: Fill the bag two-thirds with soil and plant your herbs or seeds.
steps.tip: Mint, parsley and basil grow well in bags

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old bag is now a hanging planter! Hang it by the handles on a hook outside or by a window.
steps.tip: Water a little and often — hanging pots dry out quickly

benefit: Gives a bag that's no longer used a green second life.

title: Car Seat Organizer
summary: Strap an old bag to the back of a car seat to keep things tidy.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old bag (pockets are a bonus)
- An old belt or strap
- Scissors
steps.tip: Backpacks and messenger bags have the most pockets

steps.title: Prepare the Bag
steps.heading: Open It Up:
steps.detail: Empty the bag and remove any long shoulder strap that would get in the way.
steps.tip: Keep the strap — you can reuse it in the next step

steps.title: Strap It On
steps.heading: Fix It to the Seat:
steps.detail: Loop the belt around the headrest posts, then through the bag's handles or strap loops, and buckle it tight.
steps.tip: The bag should sit flat against the back of the seat

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old bag is now a car organizer! Fill it with snacks, wipes, books or toys.
steps.tip: Works on the back of a desk chair too

benefit: A bag you no longer carry becomes useful every day.

title: Hat Plant Pot Cover
summary: Use an old hat as a soft cover for a plant pot.
materials: A plant in a small pot

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old hat (bucket hats and beanies work best)
- A potted plant that fits inside
- A small saucer
steps.tip: Pick a pot slightly smaller than the hat

steps.title: Shape the Hat
steps.heading: Fold the Brim:
steps.detail: Turn the hat upside down. Fold or roll the brim or cuff down so the hat stands upright.
steps.tip: Stuff a little paper in the bottom if the hat is too deep

steps.title: Place the Pot
steps.heading: Add the Plant:
steps.detail: Put the saucer inside the hat, then set the potted plant on it.
steps.tip: Keep the plant in its pot so watering never soaks the hat

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old hat is now a plant pot cover! Display it on a shelf or windowsill.
steps.tip: Group a few hats together for a colourful plant corner

benefit: A no-sew way to keep a hat you love on display.

title: Beanie Mug Cosy
summary: Cut the cuff of a knit beanie into a warm sleeve for your mug.
materials: Your old beanie or sweater cuff

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old knit beanie (or a sweater cuff)
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- A button
steps.tip: Thick ribbed cuffs keep drinks warm longest

steps.title: Cut the Band
steps.heading: Make the Sleeve:
steps.detail: Cut a band about 8 cm tall from the cuff of the beanie, then cut it open so it becomes a strip.
steps.tip: Stitch along the cut edges right away so the knit doesn't unravel

steps.title: Add a Button
steps.heading: Close the Cosy:
steps.detail: Wrap the strip around your mug, leaving a gap for the handle. Sew a button on one end and a thread loop on the other.
steps.tip: Make the loop snug so the cosy stays put

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old beanie is now a mug cosy! Button it around your mug and enjoy a warm drink.
steps.tip: It works on jars too — use them as pen pots

benefit: Keeps soft knit in use, even when the hat has holes.

title: Hanging Belt Shelf
summary: Use two old belts as straps to hang a wooden plank as a shelf.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Two old belts of similar length
- A wooden plank (about 60 × 15 cm)
- Four screws and a screwdriver
- Spirit level
- Pencil
steps.tip: Leather belts at least 3 cm wide hold the most weight

steps.title: Make the Loops
steps.heading: Buckle the Belts:
steps.detail: Buckle each belt to make a loop. Slide both loops onto the plank, about 10 cm from each end.
steps.tip: Check that both loops are the same size so the shelf hangs level

steps.title: Mount the Shelf
steps.heading: Fix It to the Wall:
steps.detail: Hold the shelf level against the wall, then screw the top of each belt loop into the wall. Use wall plugs if needed.
steps.tip: Check for pipes and wires before you drill

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old belts now hold a shelf! Use it for books, plants or small decorations.
steps.tip: Keep heavy things near the belts, not in the middle

benefit: Gives belts that no longer fit a stylish, useful second life.

title: Leather Cable Ties
summary: Cut a belt into small straps that keep cables and earphones neat.
tools: Leather hole punch or a nail and hammer

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old belt
- Snap fasteners or small buttons
- Sharp scissors
- Leather hole punch (or a nail and hammer)
steps.tip: Thin belts make neater ties

steps.title: Cut the Strips
steps.heading: Make Small Straps:
steps.detail: Remove the buckle, then cut the belt into 12 cm strips with rounded ends.
steps.tip: Use a coin to draw neat rounded corners

steps.title: Add the Fastener
steps.heading: Close Each Tie:
steps.detail: Punch a hole near each end and fix a snap, or sew a button on one end and cut a slit on the other.
steps.tip: Test the fit around a rolled-up cable before fixing the snap

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old belt is now a set of cable ties! Wrap them around chargers and earphones.
steps.tip: Keep one in your bag for your phone charger

benefit: Turns a cracked belt into small, long-lasting organisers.

title: Knotted Scarf Bag
summary: Fold and knot a square scarf into a bag — no sewing needed.

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail: - A square scarf (at least 70 × 70 cm)
steps.tip: Thinner, slippery fabrics knot more neatly

steps.title: Tie the Sides
steps.heading: Make the Pouch:
steps.detail: Lay the scarf flat in a diamond shape and fold it into a triangle. Tie a knot at each of the two side corners.
steps.tip: Tie the knots close to the tips so the bag is deeper

steps.title: Make the Handle
steps.heading: Knot the Top:
steps.detail: Turn the bag so the knots are inside. Tie the two remaining corners together to form the handle.
steps.tip: Untie it to wash or to wear as a scarf again

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old scarf is now a bag! Carry snacks, a book or your shopping.
steps.tip: Use it as gift wrapping too — no paper needed

benefit: A forgotten scarf becomes a zero-waste bag.

title: Skirt Apron
summary: Cut the back off a skirt or dress to make a kitchen or garden apron.
materials: Ribbon or fabric strips for ties

steps.title: Gather Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Your old skirt or dress
- Two 70 cm ties (ribbon or fabric strips)
- Fabric scissors
- Needle and thread
- Pins
steps.tip: Skirts with pockets make the most practical aprons

steps.title: Cut the Front
steps.heading: Shape the Apron:
steps.detail: Cut along both side seams and keep only the front panel. For a dress, cut at the waist and use the skirt part.
steps.tip: Keep the waistband — it becomes the top of the apron

steps.title: Hem and Add Ties
steps.heading: Finish It:
steps.detail: Fold the cut sides under 1 cm, sew them down, then sew a tie to each end of the waistband.
steps.tip: Stitch the ties in a small box for strength

steps.title: Put It to Use
steps.heading: Ready to Reuse:
steps.detail: Your old skirt is now an apron! Tie it on for cooking, painting or gardening.
steps.tip: Denim aprons are tough enough for woodwork

benefit: Turns a skirt you don't wear into something you'll use weekly.

title: Bleach Stain Design
summary: Turn a bleach stain into an intentional pattern so it looks designed, not damaged.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Bleach
- Small paintbrush
- Protective gloves
- Cardboard (to place inside the shirt)
steps.tip: Make sure the item is ready for its next use

steps.title: Create Your Design
steps.heading: Turn the stain into creative item:
steps.detail: Turn the bleach stain into a creative pattern by adding intentional bleach designs to your clothing.
steps.tip: Start with a simple pattern, such as stars, flowers, or abstract shapes

steps.title: Apply Your Pattern
steps.heading: Let’s Get Creative:
steps.detail: Use the paintbrush to carefully apply small amounts of bleach to create your chosen design on the stained area.
steps.tip: Test the bleach on a hidden area first, and avoid applying too much at once.

steps.title: Let It Set
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Allow the design to develop, then rinse and wash the garment according to its care label before wearing it again.
steps.tip: Always follow the care label and never mix bleach with other cleaning products.

benefit: A stain becomes a signature detail, so the piece stays in your wardrobe.

title: Embroidered Stain Cover
summary: Stitch a small flower, heart or star right over a stain.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Embroidery thread in 2–3 colours
- Embroidery needle
- Embroidery hoop
- Washable marker
steps.tip: Pick thread colours that already appear in your outfit

steps.title: Draw Your Motif
steps.heading: Plan the Shape:
steps.detail: Draw a simple flower, heart or star over the stain with a washable marker, a little bigger than the mark.
steps.tip: Small motifs in a cluster look intentional

steps.title: Stitch It
steps.heading: Fill It In:
steps.detail: Put the area in the hoop and fill the shape with close satin stitches until the stain is hidden.
steps.tip: Keep the stitches close together so no stain peeks through

steps.title: Finish and Wear
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Tie off on the inside, remove the hoop and rinse away the marker. Your piece is ready to wear again.
steps.tip: Wash embroidered clothes inside out on a gentle cycle

benefit: Covers a stain with something personal instead of retiring the piece.

title: Visible Mending
summary: Patch a hole with contrast stitches so the repair becomes a feature.
materials: A fabric scrap for the patch

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- A fabric scrap bigger than the hole
- Needle and contrast thread
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
steps.tip: Old jeans make great patches for other jeans

steps.title: Place the Patch
steps.heading: Cover the Hole:
steps.detail: Cut a patch 3 cm larger than the hole on every side and pin it behind the hole on the inside.
steps.tip: Round the corners so the patch doesn't peel

steps.title: Stitch the Lines
steps.heading: Make It Show:
steps.detail: Sew rows of small running stitches across the patch, 5 mm apart, through both layers.
steps.tip: Straight rows look neat; a grid looks bold — both are right

steps.title: Ready to Wear
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Trim loose threads and wear it proudly — the mend is now part of the design.
steps.tip: Add a few stitches whenever the area starts to wear again

benefit: Repairing is one of the simplest ways to keep a garment in use.

title: Fabric Paint Makeover
summary: Hide stains or scuffs — or liven up a plain piece — under a painted pattern.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Fabric paint
- Paintbrush
- Cardboard to put inside
- Washable marker
steps.tip: Wash the garment first so the paint sticks

steps.title: Sketch the Design
steps.heading: Plan It:
steps.detail: Slide cardboard inside and sketch a design that covers every stain or scuff.
steps.tip: Repeating dots or stripes are easy and hide a lot

steps.title: Paint
steps.heading: Bring It to Life:
steps.detail: Fill in the design with thin coats of fabric paint, letting each coat dry before the next.
steps.tip: Two thin coats beat one thick coat

steps.title: Set the Paint
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Let it dry for 24 hours, then iron it on the reverse side (or follow the paint's instructions) before washing.
steps.tip: Wash inside out in cold water to keep the colour bright

benefit: Gives a marked piece a new look instead of a new purchase.

title: Colour Refresh Dye
summary: Over-dye a faded or lightly stained piece in a deeper shade.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Fabric dye (darker than the garment)
- Rubber gloves
- Salt
- Bucket or washing machine
steps.tip: Natural fibres like cotton take dye best

steps.title: Prepare the Dye
steps.heading: Mix It Up:
steps.detail: Wear gloves and mix the dye with hot water and salt following the packet instructions.
steps.tip: A darker colour hides stains best

steps.title: Dye the Garment
steps.heading: Soak and Stir:
steps.detail: Wet the garment, add it to the dye bath and stir regularly for the time on the packet.
steps.tip: Stirring keeps the colour even

steps.title: Rinse It Out
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Rinse in cold water until it runs clear, then wash on its own and dry.
steps.tip: Wash it separately for the first few washes

benefit: A faded piece looks new again without buying anything.

title: Statement Patch
summary: Cover a hole or stain with a playful patch.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- An iron-on or sew-on patch
- Iron
- A thin cloth
- Needle and thread (optional)
steps.tip: Choose a patch a bit bigger than the damage

steps.title: Position the Patch
steps.heading: Find the Spot:
steps.detail: Lay the garment flat and place the patch over the hole or stain. Try it on to check the placement.
steps.tip: Slightly off-centre looks more natural

steps.title: Attach It
steps.heading: Press or Stitch:
steps.detail: Cover with a thin cloth and press with a hot iron for 30 seconds, or sew around the edge.
steps.tip: A few stitches around an iron-on patch make it last longer

steps.title: Ready to Wear
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Let it cool fully before wearing. Your piece now has a detail nobody else has.
steps.tip: Wash inside out to protect the patch

benefit: A quick fix that keeps a damaged piece in rotation.

title: Statement Button Swap
summary: Replace a lost or broken button with a fun, mismatched set.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Spare buttons (from old clothes is perfect)
- Needle and thread
- Scissors
steps.tip: Buttons from old clothes are free and unique

steps.title: Remove the Old Buttons
steps.heading: Clear the Way:
steps.detail: Carefully snip the threads of the old buttons and pull out any loose ends.
steps.tip: Keep the old buttons for another project

steps.title: Sew on the New Ones
steps.heading: Stitch Them Tight:
steps.detail: Sew each new button in the same place, passing the needle through the holes 6–8 times, then knot on the inside.
steps.tip: Wrap the thread around the base a few times so it doesn't wobble

steps.title: Button Up
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Check every buttonhole fits and wear your refreshed piece.
steps.tip: Mix sizes or colours on purpose for a bolder look

benefit: One missing button is no reason to stop wearing something.

title: Sneaker Refresh
summary: Clean, repaint scuffs and add new laces to tired shoes.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Old toothbrush and mild soap
- Fabric or leather paint
- Small brush
- New laces (optional)
steps.tip: Remove the laces before you start

steps.title: Paint the Scuffs
steps.heading: Cover the Marks:
steps.detail: Clean the shoes, let them dry, then dab paint over scuffs or add your own small design.
steps.tip: Use tape to protect the soles while painting

steps.title: Lace Them Up
steps.heading: Add New Laces:
steps.detail: Thread new laces through the eyelets — try a bright colour or a different lacing pattern.
steps.tip: Laces are the cheapest way to change a shoe's whole look

steps.title: Step Out
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Let the paint dry overnight, then wear your refreshed shoes.
steps.tip: Clean shoes regularly to keep them looking new

benefit: Keeps shoes on your feet and out of the bin.

title: Belt Refit
summary: Add a new hole so a belt fits again instead of sitting in a drawer.
tools: Leather hole punch or a nail and hammer

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Leather hole punch (or a nail and hammer)
- Ruler
- Pen
steps.tip: Measure the gap between the existing holes first

steps.title: Mark the Hole
steps.heading: Measure:
steps.detail: Wear the belt, mark where it should fasten, and match the spacing of the other holes.
steps.tip: Mark on the back so mistakes don't show

steps.title: Punch It
steps.heading: Make the Hole:
steps.detail: Punch through the mark on a firm surface, or tap a nail through with a hammer on scrap wood.
steps.tip: Protect your table with a wooden board

steps.title: Buckle Up
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Smooth the hole edges and wear your belt again.
steps.tip: Leather conditioner keeps old belts from cracking

benefit: A tiny fix that brings a belt back into use.

title: Leather Polish Revival
summary: Clean, condition and polish scuffed leather shoes, belts and bags so they look cared for again.
materials: Shoe polish in a matching colour

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Leather cleaner or saddle soap
- Leather conditioner
- Matching shoe polish
- Two soft cloths
- Old toothbrush
steps.tip: Test the polish on a hidden spot first

steps.title: Clean and Condition
steps.heading: Bring Back the Leather:
steps.detail: Brush off dirt, wipe the leather with cleaner, then rub in a thin layer of conditioner and let it soak in for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Conditioner stops dry leather from cracking further

steps.title: Polish the Scuffs
steps.heading: Cover the Marks:
steps.detail: Work a little polish into the scuffs in small circles, let it dry, then buff with a clean cloth until it shines.
steps.tip: Two thin coats look better than one thick one

steps.title: Wear It Again
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Let the polish set for an hour, then wear or carry your revived piece.
steps.tip: Polish every few months and leather can last for decades

benefit: Good leather can last for decades — a little care keeps it in use.

title: Shoe Clip Cover-Up
summary: Hide a scuff or a worn toe under a clip-on bow, brooch or fabric flower.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Two blank shoe clips or old brooches
- Fabric scraps or ribbon
- Needle and thread
- Fabric glue
steps.tip: Make the decoration bigger than the scuff it covers

steps.title: Make the Decoration
steps.heading: Create a Bow or Flower:
steps.detail: Fold a strip of fabric or ribbon into a bow, or roll it into a flower, and stitch it in the middle to hold its shape.
steps.tip: Scraps from an old garment make a matching set

steps.title: Attach the Clip
steps.heading: Fix It On:
steps.detail: Glue the bow onto the shoe clip, let it dry, then clip it over the scuff at the toe of each shoe.
steps.tip: Clips come off, so you can change the look any time

steps.title: Step Out in Style
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Wear your shoes with their new decoration — no one will know there was a scuff.
steps.tip: Move the clips to other shoes to dress them up too

benefit: A simple trick that keeps worn shoes wearable.

title: Wrapped Strap Makeover
summary: Wrap worn or peeling sandal straps in ribbon or fabric strips.
materials: Ribbon, cord or thin fabric strips

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Ribbon, cord or 1 cm fabric strips
- Fabric glue
- Scissors
steps.tip: Pick a ribbon that's slightly narrower than the strap

steps.title: Start the Wrap
steps.heading: Secure the End:
steps.detail: Glue the end of the ribbon to the inside of the strap, right where it meets the sole.
steps.tip: Hold it for a minute so the glue grips

steps.title: Wrap the Strap
steps.heading: Cover the Wear:
steps.detail: Wind the ribbon tightly around the strap, overlapping each turn slightly, until you reach the other end. Glue the end on the inside.
steps.tip: Keep every turn at the same angle for a neat finish

steps.title: Let It Dry
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Leave the sandals to dry overnight, then wear them again.
steps.tip: Seal the ribbon with fabric protector spray for summer

benefit: Keeps comfortable sandals on your feet when the straps start to wear.

title: Elbow Patches
summary: Sew classic patches over thin or worn elbows.
materials: Two patches of suede, felt or sturdy fabric

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Two oval patches (about 10 × 14 cm)
- Needle and strong thread
- Fabric scissors
- Pins
- Chalk
steps.tip: Cut patches from an old garment for a perfect match

steps.title: Place the Patches
steps.heading: Mark the Elbows:
steps.detail: Put the garment on, bend your arms and mark the elbow point with chalk. Pin a patch centred over each mark.
steps.tip: Slip a piece of card inside the sleeve so you only sew through one layer

steps.title: Sew Them On
steps.heading: Stitch Around:
steps.detail: Sew around the edge of each patch with small, even stitches, about 3 mm from the edge.
steps.tip: A blanket stitch gives a classic, hand-made look

steps.title: Wear It Proudly
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Remove the card and pins, and your garment is ready to wear again.
steps.tip: Patches protect the elbows, so the sleeves last much longer

benefit: Protects worn elbows and keeps a favourite layer in your wardrobe.

title: Frayed Fringe Hem
summary: Turn a worn or frayed hem into a deliberate fringe.

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Fabric scissors
- Ruler
- Chalk
- A pin or tweezers
steps.tip: Woven fabrics like denim fray best

steps.title: Cut a Clean Edge
steps.heading: Remove the Damage:
steps.detail: Mark a straight line just above the worn part of the hem and cut along it.
steps.tip: Try it on first so you keep the length you want

steps.title: Pull the Threads
steps.heading: Make the Fringe:
steps.detail: Use a pin or tweezers to pull out the horizontal threads along the edge, until the fringe is 2–3 cm long.
steps.tip: Stop at the same height all the way round for an even fringe

steps.title: Wash and Wear
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Wash the garment once to soften and fluff the fringe, then trim any long threads.
steps.tip: A line of stitching above the fringe stops it from growing

benefit: A worn edge becomes a style choice, so the piece stays in use.

title: New Hat Band
summary: Cover a stained or faded hat band with a ribbon, scarf or strip of fabric.
materials: Ribbon, an old scarf or a fabric strip

steps.title: Check Your Supplies
steps.heading: Prepare:
steps.detail:
- Ribbon, an old scarf or a fabric strip
- Needle and thread
- Fabric glue
- Scissors
steps.tip: Measure around the crown before cutting

steps.title: Wrap the Crown
steps.heading: Cover the Band:
steps.detail: Wrap the ribbon around the base of the crown, over the old band, and overlap the ends by 2 cm.
steps.tip: Pull it snug but not tight, so the hat keeps its shape

steps.title: Fix the Ends
steps.heading: Finish It:
steps.detail: Glue or stitch the overlap at the side, then add a small knot or bow on top to hide the join.
steps.tip: A few hidden stitches hold better than glue alone

steps.title: Ready to Wear
steps.heading: Almost There!
steps.detail: Let the glue dry, then wear your hat with its new band.
steps.tip: Swap the band to match different outfits

benefit: A quick fix that hides wear and keeps a hat in use.
